All seven certificates chain to the CA. The work is complete.

## What I did

Every channel between two Lakeside Mutual services now runs over mutual TLS, with **both ends changed together**. One private CA ("Lakeside Mutual Internal CA"), one certificate per service, each service trusting only that CA.

| Channel | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 3 backends → Customer Core | `http://…:8110` | `https://…:8110`, `client-auth=need` |
| Insurance quote events | `tcp://…:61616` | `ssl://…:61616?needClientAuth=true` |
| Policy events | `stomp://…:61613` | `stomp+ssl://…:61613?needClientAuth=true` |
| Customer data report | plaintext gRPC | gRPC over TLS, client cert required |

Application config and code only — plus `docker-compose.yml` and the run scripts. No Kubernetes manifest, no mesh. No verification was weakened anywhere: hostname verification is on for all four client ends (JDK HttpClient default, Feign with the JDK's standard verifier, `socket.verifyHostName=true` on ActiveMQ, Node/gRPC defaults). `scripts/generate-certificates.sh` is committed; its output is gitignored.

## Verified live

I started all five Java services and both Node services and exercised each channel in both the positive and negative direction. Highlights: the Customer Core returns 200 with a CA-issued client cert and rejects no-cert, rogue-CA and plaintext callers; all three Java clients (two `RestTemplate`s, one Feign) fetch from it successfully; all three TLS servers answer a certificate-less client with `tlsv13 alert certificate required`; and a `POST /policies` travelled end to end through `ssl://…:61616` → broker → `stomp+ssl://…:61613` into the Risk Management server, with the client then downloading its report over mTLS gRPC.

Then I **moved all key material out of the tree** and re-ran every suite: customer-core 26, customer-self-service 12, policy-management 19, customer-management 10 — all green, spring-boot-admin builds. No test was disabled or weakened; two test property files were updated to address the new transport.

## Two things to flag

- **Spring Boot Admin's monitoring channel is unchanged** — plaintext on both ends, not half-migrated. Its actuator targets sit on the browser-facing ports, so securing it properly would mean a separate mTLS management port on every service plus custom SBA beans; disproportionate for a tool the repo documents as "all security disabled". The visible cost: SBA can no longer scrape the Customer Core and will show it offline. This is the one service-to-service channel still in the clear, and it's stated plainly in `REFACTORING-NOTES.md`.
- **Nothing was run under Docker** (no daemon here). The compose endpoints and the NGINX load-balancing demo's `proxy_ssl_*` config are correct by construction — the certs carry the compose hostnames as SANs — but unobserved.

`REFACTORING-NOTES.md` has the full file-by-file account, the verification table, six recorded decisions, and the unverified list. One aside: the pre-existing `CustomerInformationHolderTests` failure on this machine is environmental — Maven runs on JDK 27 and Byte Buddy rejects that class file version. It fails the same way before my change; I worked around it with `-Dnet.bytebuddy.experimental=true` for my runs and changed no file for it.
